title: Start a swap box: trade what you don't use for what you need
description: A sturdy box, a simple rule — take something, leave something — and a hallway, porch or office corner. A swap box turns a street's clutter into a street's stockroom, for free.

body.heading: Set it up in fifteen minutes
paragraphs: Find a sturdy box or crate and a spot people pass: a porch, a shared hallway, a community noticeboard area — with the permission of whoever owns the space. Add a clear sign: “Swap box — take something you need, leave something clean and working.”
Seed it with three or four good things of your own: a novel, a spare mug, a working torch. A box that starts generous teaches its own manners.

body.heading: Rules that keep it lovely
paragraphs: Clean and working, only. Nothing broken, stained, unsafe or alive, and nothing so large it blocks the way. If the box overflows, the keeper — that's you, kindly — donates the surplus to a charity shop and says so on the sign.
Check the box weekly, tidy it, and remove anything unsuitable without fuss or detective work. Swap boxes run on light-touch keeping, not policing.

body.heading: Watch what it teaches
paragraphs: Within weeks you will see your neighbours' lives in cross-section: baby clothes outgrown, tools borrowed by donation, books travelling house to house. Things get used instead of stored, and nobody paid a penny.
The deepest saving is not money, though the money is real. It is the discovery that “I need a…” can be answered by the street you already live on.

takeaway: One box, one rule — take something, leave something clean and working — and a street starts sharing instead of storing.
materials: A card or small board for the sign, and a marker
Three or four clean, working items to seed the box
supervision: An adult sets up the box, gets permission for its location, and checks it weekly.
safetyNotes: Only clean, complete, working items: no medicines, sharp tools, electrical items with damaged cords, or anything unsafe for children.
Place the box where it cannot block doors, paths or fire exits, and bring it indoors in bad weather if it is not sheltered.
